9 Application provisions—former practitioners
(1) Section 92 of the Health Insurance Act 1973, as amended by this Part, applies in relation to an agreement entered into on or after the commencement of this Part, regardless of when:
the request under subsection 86(1) of that Act is made; or
the services, mentioned in paragraph 92(1)(a) of that Act, are provided; or
the person under review ceases to be a practitioner.

(2) Section 106KC of the Health Insurance Act 1973, as amended by this Part, applies in relation to a matter that a Committee becomes aware of, on or after the commencement of this Part, regardless of when:
the referral under subsection 93(1) of that Act is made; or
the services to which the referral relates are provided; or
the investigation by the Committee begins; or
the practitioner, mentioned in subsection 106KC(1) of that Act, ceases to be a practitioner.

(3) Section 106KD of the Health Insurance Act 1973, as amended by this Part, applies in relation to a draft report given to a person under review, on or after the commencement of this Part, regardless of when:
the referral under subsection 93(1) of that Act is made; or
the services to which the referral relates are provided; or
the person under review ceases to be a practitioner.

(4) Section 106L of the Health Insurance Act 1973, as amended by this Part, applies in relation to a final report given to a person under review if the relevant draft report is given to the person on or after the commencement of this Part, regardless of when:
the referral under subsection 93(1) of that Act is made; or
the services to which the referral relates are provided; or
the person under review ceases to be a practitioner.

(5) Section 106U of the Health Insurance Act 1973, as amended by this Part, applies in relation to draft determinations made on or after the commencement of this Part, and final determinations if the relevant draft determination is made on or after that commencement, regardless of when:
the referral under subsection 93(1) of that Act is made; or
the services to which the referral relates are provided; or
the person under review ceases to be a practitioner.

(6) Sections 106XA and 106XB of the Health Insurance Act 1973, as amended by this Part, apply in relation to the performance of a function or the exercise of a power on or after the commencement of this Part, regardless of:
when the practitioner, mentioned in subsection 106XA(1) or 106XB(1) or (2) of that Act, ceases to be a practitioner; or
whether the conduct mentioned in those sections is engaged in before, on or after that commencement.

(7) Section 106ZPR of the Health Insurance Act 1973, as amended by this Part, applies in relation to an agreement or a final determination that comes into effect on or after the commencement of this Part, regardless of when the person under review ceases to be a practitioner.

Repeal the subsections, substitute:
Subject to subsection (4), the other Panel members referred to in paragraph (1)(b) must also be:
if the practitioner rendered or initiated the referred services as a consultant physician in a particular specialty—consultant physicians in relation to that specialty; or
if the practitioner rendered or initiated the referred services as a specialist (other than a consultant physician) in a particular specialty—specialists in relation to that specialty; or
if the practitioner rendered or initiated the referred services as a general practitioner—general practitioners.
If the practitioner rendered or initiated the referred services as more than one kind of medical practitioner mentioned in subsection (3), then:
each other Panel member referred to in paragraph (1)(b) must be a medical practitioner of at least one of those kinds; and
those members must, in combination with each other, be medical practitioners of each of those kinds.
Example 1: A practitioner renders referred services as a consultant physician in 2 different specialties. Subsection (4) is satisfied if:
one other Panel member is a consultant physician in the first specialty and one other Panel member is a consultant physician in the second specialty; or
both other Panel members are consultant physicians in both specialties.
Example 2: A practitioner renders referred services as a consultant physician in a particular specialty and as a general practitioner. Subsection (4) is satisfied if:
one other Panel member is a consultant physician in that specialty and one other Panel member is a general practitioner; or
both other Panel members are consultant physicians in that specialty and general practitioners.
Omit “(3), (4) and (5)”, substitute “(3) and (4)”.
13 Application—inappropriate practice
Section 82 of the Health Insurance Act 1973, as amended by this Part, applies in relation to:
a request under subsection 86(1) of that Act that is made on or after the commencement of this Part; and
a referral under subsection 93(1) of that Act that is made on or after that commencement;
whether the services to which the request or referral relates are provided before, on or after that commencement.
14 Application—Professional Service Review Committee members
Section 95 of the Health Insurance Act 1973, as amended by this Part, applies in relation to a Committee set up under section 93 of that Act on or after the commencement of this Part.

hcontainer.heading: Medical examinations of persons under review

content.p: Repeal the paragraphs, substitute:
before the hearing takes place, the person gives a written notice to the Committee that includes the following:
the name of the person;
the date of the hearing;
a statement that the person has a medical condition preventing the person from appearing at the hearing or from giving evidence or answering questions in the course of the hearing;

a copy of a certificate from a medical practitioner certifying that the person has a medical condition preventing the person from so appearing or from giving evidence or answering questions and specifying the period that person is so prevented; and
the Committee is satisfied that the person has a medical condition preventing the person from appearing at the hearing or from giving evidence or answering questions in the course of the hearing.
For the purposes of determining whether it is satisfied of the matter mentioned in paragraph (5)(b), the Committee may require the person to do one or more of the following:
give specified further information to the Committee;
undergo a medical examination;
comply with any reasonable requirements of the Committee relating to the examination;
give the Committee a copy of the report by the person who conducts the examination.
Omit “him or her”, substitute “the person”.

before the hearing takes place, the officer gives a written notice to the Committee that includes the following:
the name of the officer;
the name of the body corporate;
the date of the hearing;
a statement that the officer has a medical condition preventing the officer from appearing at the hearing or from giving evidence or answering questions in the course of the hearing;

a copy of a certificate from a medical practitioner certifying that the officer has a medical condition preventing the officer from so appearing or from giving evidence or answering questions and specifying the period that officer is so prevented; and
the Committee is satisfied that the officer has a medical condition preventing the officer from appearing at the hearing or from giving evidence or answering questions in the course of the hearing.
For the purposes of determining whether it is satisfied of the matter mentioned in paragraph (4)(c), the Committee may require the executive officer to do one or more of the following:

content.p: Omit “(1) is extended”, substitute “(1), or that period as extended, is extended, or further extended,”.
Insert:
If:
during the period of 12 months referred to in subsection (1), or that period as extended, court proceedings are commenced in relation to the review; and
subsection (2) does not apply to the review;

the Director may determine, in writing, that the period of 12 months referred to in subsection (1), or that period as extended, is extended, or further extended, by a specified period that is not longer than the period for which the proceedings are on foot.
Omit “(1) is extended”, substitute “(1), or that period as extended, is extended, or further extended,”.
Insert:

If the person under review leaves Australia during the period of 12 months referred to in subsection (1), or that period as extended, the Director may determine, in writing, that the period is extended, or further extended, by a specified period that:
takes into account the period for which the person is outside Australia; and
is reasonable in the circumstances.
25 Application—power of Director to extend reviews

(1) Section 94 of the Health Insurance Act 1973, as amended by this Part, applies in relation to a decision by the Director to review the provision of services by a person made on or after the commencement of this Part.

(2) Section 94 of the Health Insurance Act 1973, as amended by this Part, also applies in relation to a decision by the Director to review the provision of services by a person made before the commencement of this Part if:
as at that commencement, the Director has not made a decision, or taken action, of the kind mentioned in paragraph 94(1)(b) of that Act; and
either of the following apply:
as at that commencement, the period of 12 months referred to in subsection 94(1) of that Act, or that period as extended, has started but not ended;

the person under review left Australia during the period of 12 months referred to in subsection 94(1) of that Act, or that period as extended, and as at that commencement has not returned to Australia.
